lesson.title: Questions in SQL
lesson.subtitle: WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, NULL, and GROUP BY in Python

video.title: Questions in SQL
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma — the maths teacher (main character)
Mr Joseph — the computer studies teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: The library; 11,000 loans; Five lines. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The librarian asked: which class borrowed the most books this term? She has eleven thousand loan records. You'll answer it in five lines.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: asking real questions in SQL, from WHERE to GROUP BY.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT title, borrowed … Caption: Five 5B loans, the newest first
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Pick rows, sort, keep a few
scenes.narration: WHERE keeps the rows you want, like class equals five B. ORDER BY sorts them, DESC for the biggest first, and LIMIT keeps the top few.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT class, COUNT(*) AS loans … Caption: The class with the most loans
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: To count per class, GROUP BY makes one row for each class, and COUNT star counts the rows in each group. Sort by that count, keep one row, and there's your answer.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Many rows → one value; They skip NULL; Except COUNT(*).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX are aggregates: they turn many rows into one value. They skip NULL, the empty value, except COUNT star, which counts every row.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! COUNT star says twelve, but COUNT of mark says eleven. Why?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: One mark is NULL: someone missed the test. COUNT star counts the row; COUNT of mark skips the empty value.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: n = {} … Caption: A dictionary: one count per class
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: What does GROUP BY do inside? Think of a dictionary: one key per class, and a running count for each. Here it is in Python, reading a CSV file.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Do the counts add up?; A group impossibly big?; Test on rows you can count.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Always judge the answer. Do the class counts add up to the school's total? Is any group impossibly big? Test your query on a few rows you can count by hand.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Run an example; AVG → MAX; Ask your own.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: ask the school database
scenes.narration: In the app, real SQLite runs on your phone. Run the examples, then change them: switch AVG to MAX, or ask which pupils live in Hilltop.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Which line keeps only the rows for class five B?

scenes.visual: Summary card: WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT; GROUP BY: a row per group; Aggregates skip NULL; Test on rows you know. Takeaway bar: A query is a question; check its answer.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: WHERE class equals five B, in single quotes. Remember: WHERE picks rows, ORDER BY sorts, and LIMIT keeps a few. GROUP BY makes one row per group, and aggregates skip NULL. And test every query on rows you can check by hand.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Three library questions; Each one in SQL. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: write three questions you'd ask your school library's database. Then write each one in SQL: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, and maybe GROUP BY.

checkpoints.prompt: COUNT(*) says 12, but COUNT(mark) says 11. Why?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — COUNT(*) counts every row; COUNT(mark) skips the NULL.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — COUNT(mark) skips empty values. One NULL mark makes it one less than COUNT(*).

checkpoints.prompt: Which line keeps only the rows for class 5B?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — WHERE keeps only the rows that match; the text goes in single quotes.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — GROUP BY makes one row per class and ORDER BY sorts. Only WHERE removes rows.
